cards.explanation: The answer is that he blesses them in a loud voice. Solomon stands up and blesses the whole assembly of Israel. I think a crowd that big needs a blessing with some volume behind it. It's a blessing for the people, spoken out loud for all of them.

The answer is True. Solomon says, "Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses." Not one, friends. He's looking at everything the LORD promised and saying every word held. That's a king with a lot to be thankful for.

The answer is that He never leaves or forsakes them. Solomon asks, "May He never leave us or forsake us." He's wishing for the LORD to stay with them, the way He was with their fathers. When you've got that, you don't need a long list of other wishes.

The answer is obedience. Solomon asks the LORD to turn their hearts to Himself "…to walk in all His ways and to keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances He commanded our fathers." The heart gets turned, and the walking follows. Obedience is what that turned heart looks like on its feet.

The answer is False. Solomon wants the LORD to uphold the cause of His servant and His people Israel "…so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God." All the peoples, friends, not only Israel. The word "only" is what makes this one false.

The answer is False. Solomon says, "So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments." The words "…as it is this day…" tell us the devotion is already there. He's not telling them to start, he's telling them to keep going.

The answer is True. Solomon offers 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep as peace offerings to the LORD. I get nervous when I bake four dozen cookies, so these numbers make my mustache curl. That's a mighty big offering.

The answer is dedicate. The text says Solomon and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD. The house is built, and now it's set apart for the LORD with these offerings. It's the moment the whole thing is given over to Him.

The answer is small. The text says the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to contain all these offerings. So Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard and offered them there. I know that feeling, friends, a batch bigger than the tray.

The answer is from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt. The text says it was a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt. That's a lot of ground for one crowd. I think a lot of people were glad to be there.
The answer is False. The text says they kept the feast before the LORD "…for seven days and seven more days—fourteen days in all." So it wasn't just seven, friends. It was double that.

The answer is joyful and glad in heart. The text says the people went home "…joyful and glad in heart…" After fourteen days of feasting, I think they might have been tired too, but the text only tells us about the joy. They left happy.

The answer is for the good the LORD did for David and Israel. The text says they were glad "…for all the good things that the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel." Their joy comes from what the LORD did. That's something worth carrying home.
